results.proposal_summary: The DigiQ Exchange Program is a student mobility funding call organised by the DigiQ Consortium (Digitally Enhanced European Quantum Technology Master project, EU Digital Europe Programme Grant No. 101084035). The call provides non-reimbursable financial support (monthly stipends) to eligible students enrolled in DigiQ-affiliated Master's programmes or recent DigiQ graduates from EU member states and DEP associated countries, enabling exchange semesters or thesis projects at partner DigiQ institutions. The total available budget is €200,000 across the consortium, with a maximum of €6,120 per student, supporting up to 55 students. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the programme end date of 30 September 2026, with a formal deadline of 1 September 2026. Applicants must contact their local DigiQ Coordinator and submit a motivation letter, CV, and course plan/learning agreement for evaluation by a local mobility committee. results.proposal_summary: PowerBoost is a targeted support stream under the EU COSME/SMP 2021-2027 programme, managed through the GreenGrid Cluster, designed to help SMEs assess their innovation readiness in the context of the energy transition. Eligible applicants are exclusively SMEs (as defined by the European Commission) established at least one year before submission. Each selected SME receives a lump-sum grant of EUR 2,000 to conduct an innovation audit identifying challenges and opportunities related to energy use, grid flexibility, sustainability, and digitalisation, resulting in a mandatory Challenge Description Report. The budget for this PowerBoost stream is EUR 100,000 in total. Applications were submitted via the EU Survey Platform by the cut-off deadline of 3 April 2026, with implementation to be completed by 31 October 2027. Successful completion of the PowerBoost stream serves as a prerequisite for eligibility in the forthcoming Solution Box Open Call, which may offer up to EUR 30,000 for piloting solutions. No co-financing is required.
results.ilo_match_evidence: This call exclusively targets SME energy innovation audits within the EU's energy transition agenda and has no alignment with ILO's mandate areas of labour standards, employment policy, social protection, or decent work.

results.proposal_summary: The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), through the UK Office for Syria, is inviting local Syrian not-for-profit and civil society organisations to submit proposals under the Syria Social Cohesion Programme: Integrated Security Fund. The programme aims to support long-term peace and stability in Syria by working with local actors, building on local knowledge, and enhancing community cohesion while reducing tensions across conflict lines. Projects must apply a gender and conflict-sensitive approach and be informed by Syrian experiences and voices. The maximum grant available is £2 million (accountable grant), with no stated minimum. The call is open only to local Syrian NGOs and civil society organisations registered in Syria with operational experience working in different governorates and a track record in social cohesion, peacebuilding, transitional justice, or gender equality. The deadline for submission is 11 September 2026 (11:59pm Beirut time) via email to isfsyria@fcdo.gov.uk. results.classification_summary: This call is ineligible on two grounds. First, the CFC's 29th Call for Proposals provides financing exclusively through loans and debt instruments (maximum USD 1.5 million), which creates a repayment obligation and does not constitute a non-reimbursable grant. Second, the eligible applicant categories are explicitly limited to SMEs, cooperatives, social enterprises, NGOs, and public or private sector entities based in CFC member countries — UN agencies and intergovernmental organisations such as the ILO are not included. Both the funding instrument and entity-type criteria fail.

ILO Eligibility.evidence: Eligible applicants are explicitly defined as 'SMEs, cooperatives, social enterprises, NGOs, and public or private sector entities' based in CFC member countries. UN agencies, intergovernmental organisations, or IGOs are not listed among eligible entity types.

results.proposal_summary: The Common Fund for Commodities (CFC) has launched its 29th Call for Proposals under the theme 'Thriving Farmers, Resilient Ecosystems, Empowered Communities', seeking applications from SMEs, cooperatives, social enterprises, NGOs, and public or private sector entities based in or operating in any of its 101 member countries. The CFC provides financing exclusively through loans and debt instruments (not grants), with a maximum of USD 1.5 million for regular projects and up to USD 300,000 under its Fast-Track procedure. Priority areas include trade finance, regenerative agriculture, local value addition, agtech, financial access for smallholders, and women's entrepreneurship; the CFC particularly encourages proposals from the Congo Basin region and Least Developed Countries. Applicants must have at least 3 years of operational history. The submission deadline is 1 October 2026, and application forms must be submitted in English.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the call touches on smallholder livelihoods, women's entrepreneurship, and decent work indicators (SDG 8 referenced in application templates), its primary purpose is commercial lending to agribusinesses rather than technical assistance or labour/social protection policy work aligned with the ILO mandate.
